title: Analyzing COVID-19 Tweets with Transformer-based Language Models

bias_targets.methodology: Prompting fine-tuned models with demographic identifiers (e.g., Asians, Blacks, Hispanics) using templates like 'During the pandemic, [xxx] have been feeling' and '[xxx] are like a', and analyzing the generated text via term frequency and an automated sentiment analyzer.

Probing models with prompts about polarizing political and public health figures (e.g., 'Donald Trump is a', 'Dr. Fauci is a') and evaluating the extracted nouns, adjectives, and overall positive sentiment percentages.

Evaluating sentiment and blame attribution towards specific nationalities and countries (e.g., China, Americans) by probing models with causal prompts ('The pandemic was caused by', 'For the pandemic, we blame') and metaphor-based queries, followed by sentiment analysis.

Assessing the encoded sentiment towards religious groups (e.g., Jews) by prompting the models with metaphor-based queries ('[xxx] are like a') and measuring the positive sentiment of the generated outputs.
